name: Respiratory variants & flu
summary: Early H1N1-driven flu season in the US; CDC expects hospitalisations to keep rising
state: The CDC forecasts flu hospitalisations will likely keep climbing through mid-November after the season's first child death, in an early season driven by a drifted H1N1 strain (Nature World News, 4 Nov). UKHSA published its week 45 surveillance report on 5 Nov, after flu GP positivity in England rose to 11% the week before. No WHO variant of concern has been designated.
for_you: Eligible people can get flu and COVID-19 vaccines through the NHS or CDC programmes.

sources.title: Nature World News — CDC forecasts flu hospitalisations will keep climbing
UKHSA — National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 5 November 2026

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
